newsitem.title: CANADA: Dominion Textile sees modest Q2 profit.
newsitem.headline: Dominion Textile sees modest Q2 profit.

text.p: Dominion Textile Inc said on Wednesday that its second quarter and full year earnings will be below market expectations because of difficult pricing conditions in basic denim and inventory adjustments.

Second quarter results to be released January 27 should show a modest profit versus a loss from continuing operations of C$0.7 million or C$0.04 a share in the year earlier period. The third quarter is also expected to be profitable, but will not likely show gains over the second quarter, the company said.
Price pressures in basic denim will continue and fourth quarter consolidated results will depend on how quickly inventory imbalances are corrected, it said.
In a statement, Dominion Textile chief executive John Boland III said excess market inventories in basic denim created price pressures.

He said the company planned to curtail production modestly in the third quarter to maintain appropriate inventory levels. It said "manufacturing variances" at its plant in Erwin, N.C. were being aggressively addressed and that the company continued to explore cost reduction and margin enhancement measures.
He said denim apparel, jeans in particular, continued to perform well at the retail level.

"Although we are encouraged by early holiday sales, it would be imprudent to expect notable market improvements until later in our fiscal year given the supply and demand environment in basic denim and the inventory adjustments required in the fashion leading segments," he said.
Boland said the company's nonwovens group showed significant improvement over the year earlier period.
